extDescription.message: Find any page you've seen before. Private and local, no account.
extDescription.description: Extension description (store short description is set separately)

searchInputLabel.description: Accessible label of the search input

onboardingConsentIntro.message: Browser Recall makes your own browsing searchable: find a page by what you remember about it, not only by its title. To do that it reads your Chrome history (page titles, addresses and visit times) once, then keeps its copy up to date.
onboardingConsentIntro.description: Consent screen: what is read and where it goes (PRODUCT_SPEC §5.1)

onboardingDeclined.message: Browser Recall will stay inactive and will not read your history. You can allow it later from this page.

onboardingImporting.message: Importing your history. You can close this page: the import continues in the background and resumes if the browser restarts.

onboardingImportedCount.description: Label before the imported page count

onboardingDone.message: Import complete. Browser Recall keeps your history up to date. Everything stays on this device.
onboardingDone.description: Shown when the import has finished

onboardingError.message: Something went wrong talking to the background service. Please reload this page.
onboardingError.description: Shown when the status request fails

searchHint.message: Type what you remember. Try site:example.com, "exact phrase", -word, when:week, is:saved.

searchNoResultsHint.message: Try fewer words, remove a filter, or turn on Deep Search to search page text.

searchError.message: Search failed. The local engine did not answer.

searchSetupNeeded.message: Browser Recall is not set up yet: it has not been allowed to read your history.

matchTitleUrl.description: Match line when the text did not match

actionForget.description: Row action: delete from Browser Recall's history copy

settingsDeepIntro.message: Deep Search lets Browser Recall also index the text of pages you open, so you can find a page by what it says. It is off by default and separate from history access. The text is stored only on this device.

settingsDeepPermission.message: Turning it on asks Chrome for permission to read the websites you visit (all http and https sites), so the text of a page can be read after it loads. You can turn it off, or remove that access in chrome://extensions, at any time; history search and remembered items keep working either way.

settingsDeepSkips.message: Skipped automatically: private windows, pages with password or payment-card fields, local and intranet addresses, non-HTML files, and sites you exclude below.

settingsDeepNoPermission.message: Chrome access to websites was removed, so Deep Search is paused.

settingsDeepNeedsConsent.message: Finish the history setup first (the Browser Recall welcome page).

settingsDeepDenied.message: Access was not granted, so Deep Search stays off.
settingsDeepDenied.description: Shown when the user denies the permission prompt

settingsDeepError.message: Something went wrong. Deep Search is unchanged.

settingsExcludeTitle.description: Heading of the excluded sites list

settingsExcludeHelp.message: Pages on these sites are never captured, and text already captured from them is deleted.

settingsClearDone.message: Deep Search text deleted. History and Saved are unchanged.

footerSettings.description: Footer link to the settings page

onboardingLocal.message: The index lives in this browser profile. There is no account, no server, no analytics and no remote AI, and the extension's own code makes no network requests. Browser Recall does not encrypt the index: anyone who can use your computer account or this browser profile can read it.

onboardingWhyHistory.message: Why the History permission: it is the only way to read titles, addresses and visit times, and to learn when you delete history so the copy can be deleted too. Chrome words this permission as being able to "change" history; Browser Recall only removes its own copy.

onboardingDeepTitle.message: Deep Search is separate and optional

onboardingDeep.message: By default only titles and addresses are searched. Deep Search can also index the text of pages you open, but it needs extra access to websites that you grant later, in Settings, with Chrome's own prompt. You can leave it off and everything else keeps working.

onboardingHowSearch.message: Search: press $1 or click the toolbar icon. If no shortcut is set, assign one on Chrome's shortcuts page.

onboardingHowSearchUnset.message: Search: click the toolbar icon, or assign a shortcut on Chrome's shortcuts page.

onboardingHowRemember.message: Remember: right-click a page and choose "Remember this page" to keep it permanently, or select text and choose "Save selection to memory". Remembered items are never expired or removed by history deletion.

settingsIndexSummary.message: $1 pages: $2 from history, $3 with page text, $4 remembered, $5 snippets.

settingsIndexUsage.message: Stored text $1 MB, database $2 MB of the $3 MB limit.

settingsIndexNoConsent.message: History access has not been allowed yet. Nothing is indexed.

settingsPausedNote.message: Indexing is paused: new history and Deep Search pages are not added. Resuming catches up on history from the paused period.

settingsMirror.message: Delete my copy when I delete history in Chrome

settingsMirrorHelp.message: Remembered pages and snippets are always kept. Chrome's own automatic expiry of old history never deletes your copy.

settingsRetention.message: Keep history and Deep Search text for

settingsRetentionHelp.message: Applied during the daily cleanup. Remembered items never expire.

settingsCapHelp.message: When the limit is reached, the oldest Deep Search text is removed first, then the oldest pages. Applied during the daily cleanup.

settingsLedgerIntro.message: Per site: how many pages are stored, how much page text, and when it last changed. Excluding a site stops Deep Search capture there and deletes its Deep Search text; deleting a site removes it from the index (remembered pages too).

settingsPageLookup.message: Show what is stored for a page address

settingsPageNone.message: Nothing is stored for that address.

settingsPageDetails.message: Visits: $1. Last visit: $2. Stored text: $3 characters. Snippets: $4.

settingsDeleteIntro.message: These actions remove data from this device only and cannot be undone.

settingsDeleteSiteSaved.message: Also delete remembered pages and snippets of that site

settingsDeleteRange.message: Delete history and Deep Search data in this date range (remembered items are kept)

settingsDeleteKeepSaved.message: Delete all history and Deep Search data, keep remembered items

settingsDeleteEverything.message: Delete everything, including remembered pages and snippets

settingsDeleteError.message: Could not delete. Nothing was changed.

settingsExportIntro.message: Exports are local files: nothing is uploaded. Chrome removes Browser Recall's data when the extension is uninstalled, so export first if you want to keep it.

settingsImportBad.message: That file is not a valid Browser Recall export. Nothing was imported.

settingsImportTooBig.message: That file is too large to import (limit 50 MB).

settingsShortcutsHelp.message: If a shortcut is not set or does not work, another extension may own it. Chrome lets you assign it yourself.

settingsAboutStores.message: Stored on this device only: titles, addresses and visit times from Chrome history; if you turn Deep Search on, the text of pages you open (up to 50 KB each); pages and text you choose to remember; settings.

settingsAboutNever.message: Never stored or sent: passwords, form contents, cookies, page images. Browser Recall has no account, backend, analytics or remote AI, and its code makes no network requests.

settingsAboutLimits.message: Not encrypted by Browser Recall: other people with access to your computer account or browser profile could read the index. Deep Search skips private windows, pages with password or payment fields, local and intranet addresses, and sites you exclude.

settingsAboutDiagHelp.message: Copies counts and settings only (no addresses, titles or text) for you to paste into a bug report. Nothing is sent automatically.

settingsError.message: Settings could not be loaded. Reload this page.

settingsSaveError.message: That change could not be saved.
